top_categories.workout_context: 60ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
At GranFondo Banff, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of GranFondo Banff. Train it until it feels boring.
5,249ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.

Road-specific control matters at GranFondo Banff. Practice on paved mountain highway through Banff National Park: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 88 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic GranFondo Banff's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before August.
At mile 60 of 88, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
5,249ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 88 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
Two threshold sessions per week without the recovery cost of VO2max work. For 88 miles, sustainable FTP gains matter more than peak power.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at GranFondo Banff. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 5,249ft of climbing on paved mountain highway through Banff National Park does to your power file on race day.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for GranFondo Banff’s 88 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Moderate altitude at GranFondo Banff. Arrive 2–3 days early. Reduce intensity expectations by 5–10%. Hydrate aggressively.
race_overlay.terrain: Mixed terrain at GranFondo Banff requires surface adaptability. Include weekly rides on paved mountain highway through banff national park to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on TT Threshold, Over Under, and G Spot to prepare you for 88 miles of paved mountain highway through banff national park in Banff, Alberta, Canada.
